gen-dafont-joystix-gf-pathway-extreme: Joystix spaces its chunky arcade letters wide apart, with stems barely heavier than the arms joining them. Pathway Extreme counters with rounded, open shapes and stubby ascenders under a big x-height, which is where it does its quiet work.
gen-dafont-joystix-gf-preahvihear: Preahvihear reads modern and lofty, its letters gaping open like a pried oyster shell. Joystix sits above it as a bold, widely tracked arcade heading, and the thin parts of its strokes stay sturdy enough to hold up against that tall, open sans.
gen-dafont-joystix-gf-pt-sans-caption: PT Sans Caption reads contemporary, with big-bodied lowercase and bowls left inviting. Joystix is best at loud, widely spaced arcade headings where heavier verticals tug against lighter horizontals, while the sans body does its best work by staying open and unfussy underneath.
gen-dafont-joystix-gf-puritan: Joystix brings bold, widely tracked arcade lettering, with a mild shift from heavy stems to lighter curves. And Puritan, a plain sans, does what the heading can't: rounded forms that stay open to the side, with oversized e and a counters.
gen-dafont-joystix-gf-questrial: Blocky arcade attitude meets a wire-thin line here, Joystix with its subtle pen-like modulation up top. And Questrial, a plain sans of single-weight strokes cut flat like stencil, would carry a long passage in a tall band with short stalks above.
gen-dafont-joystix-gf-radio-canada: Professional in manner, Radio Canada gives a plain sans line with tall, full c, s and z and a clear opening at every curve's end. And Joystix is the pair's loudest quality, its thick and thin strokes close enough to feel related in bold arcade lettering.
gen-dafont-joystix-gf-radio-canada-big: Joystix spaces its arcade letters wide, with thick and thin strokes used in moderation. Radio Canada Big does the opposite job, holding a monoline skeleton and an x-height that fills the line, with terminals finishing clear of the stem.
gen-dafont-joystix-gf-readex-pro: Readex Pro reads steady, with broad gaps at the terminals and little distance between lowercase and caps. Joystix is best at bold, widely tracked arcade display, its thinnest strokes still sturdy, while this plain sans does its best work in constant, straight-edged lines.
gen-dafont-joystix-gf-roboto: Roboto reads clean and contemporary, with generous mouths on its round letters and little gap between capital and body height. And Joystix sits over it with a steady yet faintly modulated line, bold arcade lettering spaced wide against that sans-serif.
gen-dafont-joystix-gf-ruda: Approachable is the word for Ruda, a plain sans of wire-like monoline strokes bent like thin plastic tubing. Joystix is best at bold, widely tracked arcade display with stems a little heavier than its hairlines, while Ruda's sizable x-height suits screen reading.
